subject: radiology
title: Subarachnoid Haemorrhage, Hyperdense MCA and Stroke CT Signs

steps.title: Blood fills cisterns and sulci
steps.tx: **Subarachnoid haemorrhage** paints the basal cisterns, sylvian fissures and cortical sulci bright white on non contrast CT, the pattern shown in the pictured brain scan set. Blood layered in the interpeduncular and ambient cisterns with a thunderclap headache is aneurysmal until proven otherwise. Convexity only blood over the high sulci in an older patient instead suggests amyloid angiopathy or reversible vasoconstriction syndrome.

Convexity only blood in an older patient suggests amyloid angiopathy or vasoconstriction syndrome instead.

steps.title: CT sensitivity falls with time
steps.tx: **CT sensitivity** for subarachnoid blood is highest in the first six hours, near complete with modern scanners and expert reading, then falls as blood dilutes and clears over days. A negative CT after twenty four hours therefore never closes the case when the story is thunderclap. Lumbar puncture looking for xanthochromia after twelve hours, or CT angiography in the right protocol, completes the pathway the local centre follows.

steps.title: Aneurysm shapes and sites
steps.tx: **Saccular aneurysm** balloons from branch points of the circle of Willis, anterior communicating artery commonest, then posterior communicating and middle cerebral bifurcation. The pictured aneurysm anatomy shows the sac neck and dome whose rupture fills the cisterns around its parent artery, so blood distribution hints the source: interhemispheric blood for anterior communicating, sylvian blood for middle cerebral. Posterior communicating rupture also drops a third nerve palsy beside the headache.

steps.title: Hyperdense MCA sign
steps.tx: **Hyperdense MCA sign** is a bright middle cerebral artery against darker brain and the opposite artery, fresh thrombus packed inside the vessel in acute ischaemic stroke. It predicts a large territory infarct and poor response to intravenous thrombolysis alone, pushing the team toward thrombectomy assessment. The sign must match the symptomatic side and survive comparison with calcified vessel walls, its common mimic in older patients.
steps.say: Hyperdense MCA sign is a bright middle cerebral artery from fresh thrombus packed inside it in acute stroke. It predicts a large territory infarct and pushes the team toward thrombectomy assessment. The sign must match the symptomatic side and survive comparison with calcified vessel walls.

steps.title: Early infarct signs on plain CT
steps.tx: **Insular ribbon loss** erases the normal grey white line of the insula within hours of middle cerebral occlusion, joined by lentiform obscuration and sulcal effacement over the dying cortex. Hypodensity covering more than one third of the middle cerebral territory warns against thrombolysis because haemorrhage risk climbs. ASPECTS scoring divides the territory into ten regions and subtracts one per early changed region, quantifying that judgement.

steps.title: Vasospasm and delayed deterioration
steps.tx: **Cerebral vasospasm** narrows aneurysmal arteries between days four and fourteen after the bleed, causing delayed cerebral ischaemia just when the patient seemed safe. Thick cisternal clot burden on the first scan, graded by Fisher or modified Fisher scales, predicts that risk and sets nimodipine and monitoring intensity. New deficits in the window earn transcranial Doppler velocities, CT perfusion and induced hypertension discussions with neurosurgery and neurocritical care.

Thick cisternal clot on the first scan predicts that risk. New deficits in the window earn Doppler velocities, perfusion imaging and urgent specialist discussion.

steps.title: Perimesencephalic pattern reassures
steps.tx: **Perimesencephalic haemorrhage** confines blood to the cisterns around the midbrain with at most minimal extension, normal angiography and a benign course in most patients. It lacks the diffuse sylvian and interhemispheric spread of aneurysmal rupture. One high quality negative CT angiogram, repeated per local protocol, separates it from a missed posterior circulation aneurysm, which is the one error this pattern cannot afford.

steps.title: Hydrocephalus after the bleed
steps.tx: **Acute hydrocephalus** complicates aneurysmal bleeding when blood blocks cerebrospinal fluid flow and absorption, showing enlarged temporal horns and transependymal oedema on repeat CT. Falling consciousness after initial stability is its clinical flag, and an external ventricular drain treats pressure while the aneurysm is secured. Intraventricular blood extension worsens grade and prognosis in every scoring system, so the first report must state it explicitly.
